title: Persatrix Eval-Set Recipe (RFC 0044 Phase 1)
description: The golden-trace eval-set *recipe* file shape (RFC 0044 §A). A recipe is the reproducible scenario; the expected outputs live in a sidecar `<id>.golden.yaml` (RFC 0044 §C, OQ #1). Internal-only until v1.0; `$id` may break across v0.x bumps without notice. The `tier` field selects the eval tier (RFC 0044 §F: stable | experimental | nightly), replacing the draft RFC's `target_branch` label which read misleadingly as a git branch.

id.description: EVAL-<DOMAIN>-<NNN> (RFC 0044 §E). <DOMAIN> is enforced against the flat closed list (MEMORY, RECALL, ERROR, WORKING, FACTS) — adding a domain is an RFC amendment that extends this enum. Source references live in the eval-set table, not the id.

spawned_from.description: Relative path to the manual test / RFC the recipe derives from.

tier.description: Eval tier (RFC 0044 §F). `stable` runs on every PR once its golden is recorded and verified; a fresh recipe defaults to `experimental` until it earns promotion.

seed_state.description: Scope-prefixed state keys seeded before the scenario runs (e.g. `persona:ember-owl:trust.scores.alice`).

llm_mode.description: `replay` (CI default) plays recorded responses from the golden; `live` calls a real provider (drift detection).

elapsed.description: Simulated time elapsed since the previous interaction (RFC 0044 §B). Injected into the persona temporal-awareness layer by the runner; never real wall-clock.

events.description: Per-turn event expectations (RFC 0041 typed events). Phase 1 parses and stores these but `evaluate` does NOT check them — the per-turn event stream is a runner-PR concern (PR 3, gated on RFC 0041). For event checks that run today, use top-level `assertions.event_count` / `assertions.event_sequence` against the flat run stream.

match.description: `exact` is rejected at load time for assistant/transcript content (RFC 0044 §D — LLM output is not byte-stable).

event_sequence.description: A contiguous run of event-type names expected in the flat event stream. Omit the key to not assert a sequence; an empty list asserts nothing and is rejected.

final_transcript.description: Assertions over the joined assistant transcript. Keyed by operator, so at most one `contains` and one `regex` per recipe; to require several substrings use `must_reference` (a list), not repeated `contains`.

value.description: The operand every state operator compares against. Mandatory: an omitted operand would degrade to a vacuously-passing assertion when the state key is also absent (`exact` → `None == None`), the no-vacuous-pass rule the content operators enforce (RFC 0044 §D). `required` checks key *presence*, not non-null — assert against a null/absent state value with an explicit `value: null`.
